description: We are a diverse team of passionate space enthusiasts on a mission to map the Mars. Our team combines skills in software development, data analysis, scientific research, and graphic design to create the ultimate Martian Navigation Guide. We're focused on integrating Mars terrain data, climate models, and radiation risk analysis to keep future astronauts safe. Looking for one more team member skilled in GIS/Satellite imagery and 3D visualization. Let's make interplanetary navigation a reality!
summary: Odyssey is a browser-based survival map that turns real NASA data into a safe walking route across Gale Crater. Future crews will explore Mars on foot, but the elevation, imagery, mineral and geology data they need is scattered across separate tools. Odyssey merges the MSL Gale DEM, CTX orbital imagery, 21 CRISM mineral indices, USGS geology and Curiosity photos into one interactive 3D map. An A* route planner traces the safest walk between any two points under a strict 20-degree slope limit, reporting distance, walk time, climb and slope. A first-person EVA helmet visor previews the route, and a printable mission card summarizes it. The app runs fully offline in the browser - no login, no backend - so it works where Mars work happens.
details: Odyssey is a Vite + React + TypeScript web app that renders Gale Crater as an interactive 3D terrain (vendored Three.js r128) from a local 20 m DEM (238x238 cells, ~4.7 km patch in northwest Gale near 4.80S, 137.40E). Pick a start and destination; an A* search over the slope grid traces the safest walk under a 20-degree limit, with four planner modes (Balanced, Distance, Gentler, Safest) and full route stats: distance, walk time, max/mean slope, climb, descent, warnings. Safety screening estimates walk time, suit-hours with a 25% reserve and EVA radiation dose. A first-person helmet visor walks the route with a live HUD; a printable mission card summarizes the traverse. Benefits: one map instead of five scattered datasets, fully offline with no login or backend. Working now: all of the above; demo route 3.31 km, about 2 h 46 min, 13.9-degree max slope. Limits: 20 m screening DEM, synthetic demo waypoints (not rover telemetry), safety values are unverified demo assumptions. Planned: larger coverage, live orbital data, rover-scale obstacle detection, thermal modeling.
dataRefs: 1) MSL Gale Merged DEM (Calef & Parker 2016, NASA PDS), 20 m resample - terrain elevation for the 3D map and derived hillshade/slope. 2) CTX optical mosaic via NASA Mars Trek (NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS),

orbital visual context. 3) CRISM FRT000058A3 MTRDR, 21 spectral indices (NASA/JHUAPL via PDS) - candidate mineral signatures (olivine, pyroxenes, carbonates) as map layers. 4) Curiosity (MSL) Mastcam photos
